properties.name: Authorised change intent and obligation revision
properties.subject_bearer: Change request, affected behaviour and requirements history. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.
properties.criterion: An authorised change objective and explicit preserved or revised obligations can be compared with the actual result.
properties.operating_mechanism: State the intended difference, affected obligations, legitimate decision maker and acceptance question before endorsing an intervention.
properties.trigger: A request, discovered defect or environmental pressure proposes changing an existing commitment.
properties.non_trigger_cheap_path: A short accepted issue with concrete examples is enough for a bounded low-risk change; reject or defer an unjustified request.

conditions: Decision authority and domain meaning must be established; disputed intent cannot be resolved by test count.
required_inputs.interpretation: Related obligations and prerequisites, not a serial scheduling graph. Typed relations in the composition model control the relationship meaning.

properties.outputs_evidence_constraints: An authorised change objective and explicit preserved or revised obligations can be compared with the actual result.

consumer.consumer: Those entitled to request or rely on the behaviour, not merely the test author.
consumer.decision: An authorised change objective and explicit preserved or revised obligations can be compared with the actual result.

authority.actors: Those entitled to request or rely on the behaviour, not merely the test author.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

communication_interaction.exchange: Change request, affected behaviour and requirements history.
communication_interaction.purpose: Enable the stated consumer to judge the mechanism, assumptions and postcondition. Use the cheapest adequate channel in NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH; mere publication is not successful communication.

ACCOUNT.critical_assumption: Decision authority and domain meaning must be established; disputed intent cannot be resolved by test count.
ACCOUNT.discriminating_question: Which affected stakeholder is missing from the stated acceptance question?

ACCOUNT.needed: An identifiable baseline, affected interests and an actor entitled to resolve the objective; emergency delegation must be explicit.
ACCOUNT.failure_test: Approval can institutionalise an obsolete requirement, exclude affected users or become a bottleneck; procedural approval is not evidence that the goal is beneficial.
ACCOUNT.cheap_or_nontrigger: Use an existing unambiguous authorised request; no new board or document is needed. Decline changes without a supported objective.

costs_failure_modes.controlled_failure: An accepted or executed change does not correspond to a legitimate supported objective, or preservation is silently substituted for an authorised behavioural change.

FINDINGS: Source-supported: issue/PR/test disagreement can leave correctness indeterminate. Analytical: a formal approval can still exclude affected people.
Approval can institutionalise an obsolete requirement, exclude affected users or become a bottleneck; procedural approval is not evidence that the goal is beneficial.
This is an analytical decision model, not a proof that stakeholder agreement produces a beneficial objective. Swanson and Chapin body-access limits preclude detailed original-taxonomy claims.

coupling_costs: A mistaken objective can contaminate correct analysis.
Metric or population drift can mimic changing value.
Historical intention may remain indeterminate.
Alerts without a capable consumer accumulate noise.
The wrong test ritual can miss operative enforcement.
Deceptive suggestions can increase review burden and survive shared oracles.
Emergency labels can launder feature removal or indefinite suspension.
Local success can hide mismatched identities or permissions.
Meta-governance can consume the capacity it is meant to protect.
Compatibility layers can preserve defects indefinitely.
Duplicated approval adds ceremony if the boundaries are already jointly satisfied.
Normative ambiguity may persist after more testing.
Over-simplification can omit a genuinely multi-party decision.

ACCOUNT.discriminator: Identify the actual obligation, consumer and authorisation for revision; unresolved authority blocks that revision, not unrelated work.
ACCOUNT.hybrid_failure: Two ambiguous meanings, unmaintained compatibility mode, or an oracle changed solely to pass.

ACCOUNT.analytical_adjudication: Approval can institutionalise an obsolete requirement, exclude affected users or become a bottleneck; procedural approval is not evidence that the goal is beneficial.

selection_limits.ACCOUNT: ESME-T001: Continuity versus necessary behavioural change. Preserve behaviour with a current supported consumer; change it when legitimate intent is revised and transition consequences are addressed. A failing characterisation test is a question, not automatic veto.

retirement_omission_condition.CANONICAL: Omit a mechanism when its trigger is absent or a cheaper adequate substitute establishes the actual obligation; retire it when its protected obligation or consumer ends. Do not use omission to waive an unchanged supported outcome.

INPUT_SPECIFIC.CONDITIONS: A short accepted issue with concrete examples is enough for a bounded low-risk change; reject or defer an unjustified request. Omit or retire a control when its protected obligation, relevant failure mechanism or decision consumer no longer exists; record unresolved support consequences before removing it.
Compare change with continued useful operation and retirement. End a classification or approval artefact when no consumer uses its distinction, while preserving any actual authorisation requirement.
